issue_context.title: Todoist integration doesn't respect local time zone
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Events in Todoist are all stored in UTC, but the user has the option of setting a local time zone in their account. Home Assistant creates a calendar from the items on the task list, and gives the calendar an "overdue" attribute which is true if the top item is overdue, and a "due-today" attribute. Oddly, the "overdue" attribute will return 'true' if the task is overdue by even a minute, and respects local time. However, the "due-today" attribute does not seem to behave this way. 

In the yaml snippet below everything is working as expected because I'm on CDT U.S. time; however once UTC rolls over to the next day, "due-today" will resolve as 'false'.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

 core-2021.11.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

 core-2021.11.1

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

todoist

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/todoist/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
message: Get Ready for School (Get Dressed, Brush Teeth, Finish Breakfast)
all_day: false
start_time: '2021-11-15 12:28:04'
end_time: '2021-11-15 13:30:00'
location: ''
description: https://todoist.com/showTask?id=redacted
due_today: true
overdue: false
all_tasks:
  - Get Ready for School (Get Dressed, Brush Teeth, Finish Breakfast)
  - Feed cat
  - >-
    Homework Notebook— Complete Homework —-Repack Homework AND school iPad in
    your backpack.
  - Put away clean dishes (if any)
  - Scoop Kitty Litter
  - Put your lunchbox and water bottle on the counter
  - Hang up your backpack, put used mask in bucket, shake sand out of shoes
  - Take a Bath or Shower
  - Get Ready for Bed (Brush Teeth, Put on Pajamas)
priority: 4
labels:
  - kids
friendly_name: Kids's jobs
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_
comments:
Hey there @boralyl, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`todoist`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L543) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

@lymanbuttler Thanks for taking the time to report an issue.  Dates/times/timezones can be very tricky so I wanted to make sure I understand the problem fully.  

In your example you have set a specific end time in your local time zone (CST). Since the timezone difference between UTC is 6 hours, are you saying that at 6pm CST - 11:59pm CST that your task no longer has the `due_today` attribute as `true`, but is instead `false`?

Thanks @boralyl for maintaining this. Yes time zones are tricky so I'm not even completely sure my understanding of the problem is correct, but yes, your description sounds exactly like what I'm seeing. Maybe the way "overdue" is handled could offer clues, since that seems to work fine.

@lymanbuttler Thanks for the clarification.  I think I've found the issue.  For the `due_today` attribute we are comparing the task due date (in UTC) to the current date (in local time, not UTC, unless your environment happens to be configured to use UTC as your local time).

review_comments: Per the [documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime.today), `datetime.today` returns the current datetime in the local timezone.  This is fine if your local timezone is UTC, but if it's anything else, this check would fail in cases where the UTC date was different that the local timezone date.  `task[END]` is always UTC.
